en: Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Al-Tufayl and his companions arrived and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Daws has disbelieved and refused [to obey], so supplicate Allah against them!' It was said: 'Daws is ruined!' But he said: 'O Allah, guide Daws and bring them [to Islam].'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Mughirah, from 'Amir, from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: I came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he said to me: 'Indeed, the first charity that brightened the face of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and the faces of his Companions was the charity of Tayyi' that you brought to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kuraib narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Bakr's; they said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Tell me, if Juhaynah, Aslam, and Ghifar are better than Banu Tamim, Banu 'Abdullah ibn Ghatafan, and 'Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah...' and he prolonged his voice with it. They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, then they are ruined and lost!' He said: 'Indeed, they are better.' And in the narration of Abu Kuraib: 'Tell me, if Juhaynah, Muzaynah, Aslam, and Ghifar...'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Harun ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us; they said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us; (H) and 'Amr al-Naqid narrated it to me: Shababah ibn Sawwar narrated to us; they said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, with this chain of transmission.

Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'Aslam, Ghifar, Muzaynah, and Juhaynah are better than Banu Tamim, Banu 'Amir, and the two confederates: Banu Asad and Ghatafan.'

Harun ibn 'Abdullah narrated to me: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'qub al-Dabbi, the chief of Banu Tamim, narrated to me, with this chain of transmission, the like of it, and he said: 'and Juhaynah,' without saying 'I think.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shu'bah; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us; they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Ya'qub: I heard 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah narrating from his father that al-Aqra' ibn Habis came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: 'Only the thieves of the pilgrims from Aslam, Ghifar, Muzaynah—and I think Juhaynah (Muhammad is the one who was uncertain)—have pledged allegiance to you.' Thereupon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Tell me, if Aslam, Ghifar, Muzaynah—and I think Juhaynah—are better than Banu Tamim, Banu 'Amir, Asad, and Ghatafan, have they been ruined and lost?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, they are indeed better than them.' And in the hadith of Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Muhammad is the one who was uncertain' is not mentioned.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ya'qub al-Dawraqi narrated to me; they said: Isma'il—meaning Ibn 'Ulayyah—narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, Aslam, Ghifar, and some from Muzaynah and Juhaynah—or some from Juhaynah and Muzaynah—are better in the sight of Allah (he said: I think he said: on the Day of Resurrection) than Asad, Ghatafan, Hawazin, and Tamim.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Mughirah—meaning al-Hizami—narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said; (H) and 'Amr al-Naqid, Hasan al-Hulwani, and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us; 'Abd said: 'informed me' and the other two said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih, from al-A'raj, who said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, Ghifar, Aslam, Muzaynah, and whoever is from Juhaynah—or he said: Juhaynah and whoever is from Muzaynah—are better in the sight of Allah on the Day of Resurrection than Asad, Tayyi', and Ghatafan.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us; Ibn al-Muthanna said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, who said: I heard Abu Salamah narrating from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: 'Aslam, Ghifar, Muzaynah, and whoever is from Juhaynah—or Juhaynah—are better than Banu Tamim, Banu 'Amir, and the two confederates: Asad and Ghatafan.'

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, with this chain of transmission, the like of it, except that in the hadith: Sa'd said regarding some of this: 'as far as I know.'

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Quraysh, the Ansar, Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, Ghifar, and Ashja' are my allies; they have no protector besides Allah and His Messenger.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Yazid—who is Ibn Harun—narrated to us: Abu Malik al-Ashja'i informed us, from Musa ibn Talhah, from Abu Ayyub, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Ansar, Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Ghifar, Ashja', and whoever is from Banu 'Abdullah are my allies to the exclusion of other people, and Allah and His Messenger are their protectors.'

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated it to me: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated to us: Harb ibn Shaddad narrated to us, from Yahya: Abu Salamah narrated to me: Ibn 'Umar narrated to me, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say... the like of the hadith of these narrators from Ibn 'Umar.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah narrated to us; (H) and 'Amr ibn Sawwad narrated to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Usamah informed me; (H) and Zuhayr ibn Harb, al-Hulwani, and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me, from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd: my father narrated to us, from Salih; all of them from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it. And in the hadith of Salih and Usamah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said that upon the pulpit.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us; Yahya ibn Yahya said: 'informed us', and the others said: Isma'il ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, that he heard Ibn 'Umar saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Ghifar—may Allah forgive them; Aslam—may Allah keep them safe; and 'Usayyah has disobeyed Allah and His Messenger.'

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from al-Layth, from 'Imran ibn Abi Anas, from Hanzalah ibn 'Ali, from Khufaf ibn Iyma' al-Ghifari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said in a prayer: 'O Allah, curse Banu Lihyan, Ri'l, Dhakwan, and 'Usayyah; they disobeyed Allah and His Messenger. Ghifar—may Allah forgive them; and Aslam—may Allah keep them safe.'

Husayn ibn Hurayth narrated to me: al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, from Khuthaym ibn 'Irak, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Aslam—may Allah keep them safe; and Ghifar—may Allah forgive them. Indeed, I did not say it, but Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, said it.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, Ibn Bashshar, Suwayd ibn Sa'id, and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us; they said: 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah; (H) and 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us; they said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Shababah narrated to us: Warqa' narrated to me, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah; (H) and Yahya ibn Habib narrated to us: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Abu 'Asim; both of them from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir; (H) and Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me: al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us: Ma'qil narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir; all of them reporting from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'Aslam—may Allah keep them safe; and Ghifar—may Allah forgive them.'
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated it to us; they said: Abu Dawud narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, in this chain of transmission.

'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar all narrated to us from Ibn Mahdi; Ibn al-Muthanna said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to me: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to me: 'Go to your people and say: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: Aslam—may Allah keep them safe; and Ghifar—may Allah forgive them.'

Haddab ibn Khalid narrated to us: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us: Humayd ibn Hilal narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Samit, who said: Abu Dharr said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Ghifar—may Allah forgive them; and Aslam—may Allah keep them safe.'

Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar all narrated to us from Ibn 'Ar'arah—and the wording is al-Jahdami's: Muhammad ibn 'Ar'arah narrated to me: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: I set out with Jarir ibn 'Abdullah al-Bajali on a journey, and he used to serve me. So I said to him: 'Do not do that.' He said: 'I have seen the Ansar do something for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), so I took an oath that I would not accompany anyone from among them except that I would serve him.' Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar added in their hadith: 'and Jarir was older than Anas,' and Ibn Bashshar said: 'more advanced in age than Anas.'

'Amr al-Naqid and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me; they said: Ya'qub—who is Ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd—narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab; he said: Abu Salamah and 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah ibn Mas'ud said that they heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said while in a large gathering of Muslims: 'Shall I tell you about the best of the clans (houses) of the Ansar?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal.' They said: 'Then who, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Then Banu al-Najjar.' They said: 'Then who, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Then Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj.' They said: 'Then who, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Then Banu Sa'idah.' They said: 'Then who, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Then in all the clans of the Ansar there is good.' Thereupon Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah stood up angered and said: 'Are we the last of the four?' when the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) named their clan, and he wished to speak to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). Some men of his people said to him: 'Sit down! Are you not pleased that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) named your clan among the four clans that he named? Those he left out without naming are far more than those he named.' So Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah refrained from speaking to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).

'Amr ibn 'Ali ibn Bahr narrated to us: Abu Dawud narrated to me: Harb ibn Shaddad narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir: Abu Salamah narrated to me that Abu Usayd al-Ansari narrated to him that he heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: 'The best of the Ansar,' or 'The best of the clans of the Ansar,' like their hadith in mentioning the clans, and he did not mention the story of Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah (may Allah be pleased with him).

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi narrated to us: al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed us, from Abu al-Zinad; he said: Abu Salamah testified that he heard Abu Usayd al-Ansari testifying that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The best clans of the Ansar are Banu al-Najjar, then Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, then Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, then Banu Sa'idah, and in all the clans of the Ansar there is good.' Abu Salamah said: Abu Usayd said: 'Am I to be suspected regarding the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)? If I were a liar, I would have begun with my own people, Banu Sa'idah!' That reached Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, and he felt aggrieved within himself and said: 'We have been placed behind, so that we are the last of the four! Saddle my donkey so that I may go to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).' His nephew Sahl spoke to him and said: 'Are you going to object to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) when the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) knows best? Is it not sufficient for you to be the fourth of four?' So he relented and said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best,' and he ordered that his donkey be unsaddled.

Muhammad ibn 'Abbad and Muhammad ibn Mehran al-Razi narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn 'Abbad's: Hatim—who is Ibn Isma'il—narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Humayd, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Talhah, who said: I heard Abu Usayd delivering a sermon before Ibn 'Utbah, and he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The best clans of the Ansar are the clan of Banu al-Najjar, the clan of Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, the clan of Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, and the clan of Banu Sa'idah.' Abu Usayd said: 'By Allah, if I were to favor anyone with it, I would have favored my own kinsfolk.'

Qutaybah and Ibn Rumh narrated to us from al-Layth ibn Sa'd; (H) and Qutaybah narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us; (H) and Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us; they said: 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us; all of them from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it, except that he does not mention the statement of Sa'd in the hadith.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us: Abu Dawud narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah: I heard Anas narrating from Abu Usayd al-Ansari, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), similar to it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's; they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: I heard Qatadah narrating from Anas ibn Malik, from Abu Usayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The best clans of the Ansar are Banu al-Najjar, then Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, then Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, then Banu Sa'idah, and in all the clans of the Ansar there is good.' Thereupon Sa'd said: 'I see that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) has preferred others over us!' So it was said to him: 'He has indeed preferred you over many!'
